corrected_domain_note: Substance is data-integrity / availability reachable only by an authenticated admin (no RBAC exists, so 'authz' here means 'authz boundary was not crossed'; the impact is real but is not an authorization bypass).
category: data-integrity / availability (credential destruction + defeat of both recovery mechanisms)
severity_rationale: Authed-but-severe: mass, silent, permanent loss of every upstream provider credential, converting the two intended safety nets (backup restore, config rollback) into the destruction vector. Above medium because the codebase explicitly denies an admin the equivalent power through sanctioned CRUD (providers.go:111 empty-api_key guard; providers.go:137-141 delete blocked while a provider is referenced by an alias), so restore/rollback is the only path able to blank keys of in-use providers, and the loss is unrecoverable from any backup, version snapshot, or operation log. Not critical: requires an admin JWT, no privilege bypass, and no exfiltration.
title: Config restore / rollback wipes the providers table and recreates rows without APIKeyEnc, permanently destroying all upstream provider credentials while the UI keeps showing a healthy masked key
function: (*Manager).RestoreBundle (wipe at bundle.go:86, keyless recreate at bundle.go:90-91); callers Rollback (bundle.go:162) and admin.restoreBackup (backend/internal/admin/backup.go:81)
evidence: backend/internal/model/model.go:107 — `APIKeyEnc    string    `gorm:"type:text" json:"-"` // AES-GCM 加密存储 (REQ-005 ④)` : the ciphertext is invisible to encoding/json, so ConfigBundle can never carry it.

backend/internal/runtime/bundle.go:15 — `// ConfigBundle 可序列化的全量配置（密钥保持 DB 原样密文，跨版本/备份一致）。` : the author's stated intent (ciphertext preserved across backups/versions) is contradicted by the json:"-" tag above.

backend/internal/runtime/bundle.go:81-86 — `for _, table := range []any{` / `&model.Provider{}, &model.AliasUpstream{}, &model.ModelAlias{},` / ... / `if err := tx.Where("1 = 1").Delete(table).Error; err != nil {` : hard delete of every provider row (no gorm.DeletedAt on model.Provider, no GORM hooks — verified by grep).

backend/internal/runtime/bundle.go:90-91 — `if len(b.Providers) > 0 {` / `if err := tx.Create(&b.Providers).Error; err != nil {` : re-insert of rows deserialized from bundle JSON, where APIKeyEnc is the zero value "".

backend/internal/admin/backup.go:31 — `body, _ := json.Marshal(b)` (createBackup) and backend/internal/admin/configstatus.go:68 — `body, _ := json.MarshalIndent(b, "", "  ")` (exportConfig) and backend/internal/runtime/manager.go:386 — `if b, err := json.Marshal(bundle); err == nil {` (recordVersion -> ConfigVersion.SnapshotJSON) : all three persistence paths for snapshots/backups drop APIKeyEnc at marshal time (ExportBundle loads it from DB at bundle.go:32, so the loss is in Marshal, not in the query).

backend/internal/runtime/manager.go:214-218 — `if plain, err := m.enc.Decrypt(p.APIKeyEnc); err == nil {` / `p.APIKey = plain` / `p.APIKeyEnc = ""` / `} else {` / `p.APIKey = "" // 解密失败：保留空密钥，该上游调用时会失败` : Decrypt("") errors (crypto/crypto.go:49-51 `if len(raw) < ns { return "", errors.New("ciphertext too short") }`), so the reloaded snapshot carries an empty key while the provider stays routable (manager.go:236-239 filters only missing/disabled providers; manager.go:244-246 copies APIKey into ResolvedUpstream).

backend/internal/gateway/gateway.go:507 — `req, err := adapter.BuildUpstreamRequest(up.Protocol, cr, up.UpstreamModel, up.BaseURL, up.APIKey)` with backend/internal/adapter/adapter.go:560 — `req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+apiKey)` and adapter.go:679 — `req.Header.Set("x-api-key", apiKey)` : no fail-closed guard on an empty upstream credential; the gateway forwards no credential and the upstream answers 401/403.

backend/internal/model/model.go:109 — `APIKeyMasked string    `gorm:"size:64" json:"api_key_masked"`` : the masked key DOES round-trip through bundles, so backend/internal/admin/providers.go:34-45 listProviders keeps returning a plausible masked value and frontend/src/pages/providers/Providers.tsx:246 `dataIndex: 'api_key_masked'` keeps rendering it — the wipe looks healthy.

backend/internal/admin/routes.go:139 — `api.POST("/config/rollback", s.AuthMiddleware(), s.rollbackConfig)` and routes.go:147 — `api.POST("/backups/restore", s.AuthMiddleware(), s.restoreBackup)` with backend/internal/admin/middleware.go:14-33 (JWT check only, no role/RBAC anywhere in the admin surface): both destruction paths need only a valid admin session.

backend/internal/health/health.go:116-125 — `func (c *Checker) apiKey(p model.Provider) string {` / `if p.APIKeyEnc == "" {` / `return ""` and health.go:4-6 `任何 HTTP 响应（含 401/403/404）= 端点可达 = 健康` : the periodic probe sends no Authorization after the wipe and still calls `c.bl.RecordSuccess(p.ID)` (health.go:113), so dashboard upstream_health stays green.
backend/internal/audit/audit.go:110-123 — `b, err := json.Marshal(v)` into BeforeJSON/AfterJSON : operation logs also exclude APIKeyEnc, so no audit row retains a recoverable copy.

backend/internal/admin/providers.go:111 — `if req.APIKey != "" {` and providers.go:137-141 — `s.db.Model(&model.AliasUpstream{}).Where("provider_id = ?", id).Count(&count)` / `if count > 0 { s.fail(c, 409, 40901, "该供应商仍被模型别名引用，无法删除")` : the invariant 'a referenced provider keeps its credential' is deliberately enforced by CRUD and only restore/rollback violates it.
attack_path: 1. Attacker holds/impersonates an admin session (valid HS256 JWT from /auth/login). No additional privilege needed and none lacking.

2. POST /api/admin/v1/config/rollback with body {} -> rollbackConfig (admin/configstatus.go:52-60) -> Manager.Rollback (bundle.go:146) which needs >=2 status='ok' ConfigVersion rows — satisfied automatically because every Reload writes one (manager.go:389-391).
3. json.Unmarshal of target.SnapshotJSON (bundle.go:156) yields Providers with APIKeyEnc="" (the row was marshalled with json:"-").

4. RestoreBundle: DELETE FROM providers WHERE 1=1 (bundle.go:86) then INSERT keyless rows (bundle.go:91) inside the same committed transaction; Bump + Reload (bundle.go:165-166) replaces the live snapshot with empty-key providers.

5. All gateway traffic (/v1/chat/completions, /v1/responses, /v1/messages) now reaches upstream with an empty credential -> 401/403 for every model. APIKeyMasked still displays and upstream_health still reports healthy, so the cause is hidden.

Alternative trigger, equally destructive and operator-normal: POST /api/admin/v1/backups (creates a keyless JSON, admin/backup.go:25-43) then POST /api/admin/v1/backups/restore {"id":N} (backup.go:66-72 `data = r.Content`) — restoring a freshly and legitimately created backup by ID is enough. A supplied {"content":...} of any exported config.json works too.
impact: Every activation of either safety net (restore by ID, restore by supplied content, one-click rollback) hard-deletes and recreates all provider rows without their AES-GCM ciphertext. Result: total credential outage for every upstream provider — the gateway keeps routing (Enabled round-trips) but authenticates to vendors with an empty key, so all model traffic fails upstream. The loss is unrecoverable from any backup, config version snapshot, or operation log, because no JSON serialization of ConfigBundle/Provider ever included APIKeyEnc; the only fix is manually retyping every provider key. Visibility is actively misleading: the UI keeps showing api_key_masked, health checks record success on the resulting 401s, and the rollback confirmation copy promises 'This restores the previous version of all provider/model/guardrail/quota config' (frontend/src/i18n/locales/en-US/pages/configStatus.ts:9) without mentioning credentials. Secondary value to a hostile admin: a deniable mass-sabotage primitive whose audit trail is just action=restore/rollback with before=nil/after=nil (admin/backup.go:85, admin/configstatus.go:58).
mitigations_checked: Gateway tenant API keys are NOT destroyed: RestoreBundle (bundle.go:79-143) never writes or clears api_keys, so ConfigBundle.APIKeys (bundle.go:24) is inert, and Quota/RateLimitRule api_key_id references (model.go:179, model.go:197) remain valid; KeyHash is json:"-" (model.go:37).

No credential exfiltration in the reverse direction: because APIKeyEnc is json:"-", backups, GET /config/export, the /backups/:id/download artifact and operation-log before/after payloads all omit provider secrets — this bug destroys rather than leaks.

Alias upstream references are rebuilt consistently: provider IDs round-trip (model.go:103 `json:"id"`) and AliasUpstream rows are re-keyed to new alias IDs (bundle.go:101-109), so the failure is credential-only, not referential.

Both endpoints are authenticated (routes.go:139/147 + middleware.go:14-33) and there is no CSRF/CORS shortcut (same-origin SPA, no CORS middleware), so an unauthenticated attacker cannot trigger the wipe directly.

Rollback does require >=2 'ok' ConfigVersion rows (bundle.go:151-153), so a virgin install with <2 reloads errors instead — but Reload writes a version every time, so this never protects a running system.

Reload is fail-open on decrypt errors (manager.go:217-218 keeps the provider with an empty key rather than dropping it), which is what makes the outcome 401s from the vendor instead of an obvious 'no upstream configured' error; no fail-closed guard exists in gateway.go:507 / adapter.go:560 / adapter.go:679.

No regression test guards this path (grep `func Test.*(Backup|Bundle|Rollback|Restore)` -> no matches) and no doc/PRD note acknowledges the limitation, so bundle.go:15 remains a false assertion rather than a documented tradeoff.
recommendation: Two-part fix. (1) Make the secret round-trip explicitly: define a dedicated bundle transport struct that carries api_key_enc (or a keyring section) so ConfigVersion snapshots, backups and exports are actually restorable, while keeping the provider API list responses ciphertext-free (listProviders already returns model.Provider with json:"-", so the field must be added only to the bundle path). (2) Until then, make RestoreBundle refuse to blank credentials: before the delete loop, read existing api_key_enc into a map by provider ID, and either skip recreation of providers whose bundle entry has an empty APIKeyEnc (upsert the non-secret columns instead of delete+create) or abort with a clear error naming the providers that would lose keys; also update the rollback/restore confirmation copy to state the credential consequence. Add a regression test asserting provider count AND non-empty APIKeyEnc after an export -> restore -> rollback cycle, and add a startup/health warning that lists providers whose APIKeyEnc is empty (health.go:118 already has that predicate; surface it in /config-status instead of recording the probe as success).

verification_record.quotes_verified: Every verbatim quote in the original finding matched at the stated line, including runtime/manager.go:386 and manager.go:214-218; no wrong-line or fabricated evidence.
verification_record.line_pin: Primary line 86 is correct (the destructive DELETE); the credential loss completes at line 91 (the keyless Create).
verification_record.path_correction: The finding cites backup.go / configstatus.go without a package path (implying backend/internal/handler/, which does not exist). Actual files are backend/internal/admin/backup.go and backend/internal/admin/configstatus.go; line numbers are unchanged.
impact_precision_corrections: 'records no evidence of the wipe' should read 'records the action (restore/rollback) but with nil before/after state, so no evidence of what was destroyed'.
'silent outage' should read 'silent as to cause': the failure is loud to clients and CallLog rows, but api_key_masked and upstream_health both keep reporting healthy.
'rollback is a one-click button' is accurate but the button does carry a Popconfirm (frontend/src/pages/settings/ConfigStatus.tsx:102-108) whose copy misleads rather than warns.
new_evidence_added_by_verifier: providers.go:111 and providers.go:137-141 prove the codebase deliberately protects APIKeyEnc of referenced providers from blanking/deletion, so restore/rollback is the only path that can erase an in-use credential — this is the privilege delta that keeps severity at high.
health.go:116-125 + health.go:4-6 + health.go:113 prove the periodic probe still records success after keys are wiped, so the damage is invisible to the product's own liveness telemetry.
crypto.go:43-51 proves Decrypt("") returns 'ciphertext too short' rather than ('', nil), confirming the manager.go:217-218 empty-key branch specifically.
audit.go:110-123 proves operation-log before/after payloads also exclude APIKeyEnc, closing the last possible recovery path and confirming 'unrecoverable'.
Grep proves there is no custom MarshalJSON and no alternate export struct carrying api_key_enc, and that no test exercises RestoreBundle/ExportBundle.
